decisions.reason: As a core airfield-control hardware extension with long airport procurement cycles and strong fit to the installed base, its option value still outweighs the carrying cost.
This surveillance display supports the firm's integrated tower and airfield offering, and the uncertainty around wider adoption still justifies keeping it in the portfolio.
A training program is inexpensive to carry, complements complex airport systems sales, and preserves service-side upside with little downside risk.
Although this narrower lighting course is easier to discontinue and may have more limited demand, it is low-cost and still valuable as a complementary option around the firm's airfield base.
Collaboration software is closely aligned with the firm's stated move toward integrated, real-time and data-driven airport operations, so management would be reluctant to abandon it early.
Because this MLAT system is presented as a flagship in the firm's strategic direction, management is likely to continue backing it despite higher resource needs.
